question.text: To a 10 ml, 1M aqueous solution of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> , excess of NaOH is added so that all <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> is disproportionated to <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msubsup></math> . The resulting solution is made free of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> by extraction and excess of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> is neutralised by acidifying the solution. The resulting solution is sufficient to react with 2g of impure <math><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></math> (M = 128 g/mole) sample. Which of the following is the correct % purity of oxalate sample
